touren.kurz: A new empty script, an affect block for one figure and a first command inside it.

classic.text: **Open an empty tab.** Click the **+** at the end of the tab bar (or **{{MenuFile}} → {{FileNew}}**). A new tab `unnamed.txt` opens with an empty script. The mode bar on the left must be on **{{ViewEvents}}** - then the **{{GroupEvents}}** list with every command is on the left.
classic.unter: The + at the end of the tab bar opens an empty script.

classic.text: **Find affect in the list.** The **{{GroupEvents}}** list shows every command of the game with its values. `affect` is near the top. Hover over it to read what it does.
classic.unter: affect in the Events list.

classic.text: **Double-click it.** `affect` appears in the script tree in the middle. It is already open (the box in front shows a minus), because a block holds other commands.
classic.unter: The new affect block in the tree.

classic.text: **Name the figure.** Double-click the new line (or select it and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>). The **{{EditorTitle}}** opens. Type the name of the figure into the first field - with a map loaded, the small arrow next to it lists every name of the map. Leave `FLUSH` in the second field and press **{{EditorOk}}**.
classic.unter: The event editor for affect: the name field and Ok.

classic.text: **Select the block, then pick the next command.** Click the `affect` line once (1). Then double-click `wait` in the list (2). Because the selected block is open, the command goes to the start of the block.
classic.unter: 1: the selected affect block. 2: wait in the list.

classic.text: **Check the result.** `wait` now sits inside the block, indented under `affect`. Commands you insert after it follow it, in order, inside the same block.
classic.unter: wait inside the affect block.

classic.text: **Save.** Press **{{FileSave}}** in the action column on the right (or <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>S</kbd>). The first time, behaved asks for a name - script names are lower case without spaces, for example `my_first.txt`.
classic.unter: Save in the action column.

touren.titel: Three ways to add a command
touren.kurz: Double-click, drag and drop, or the Insert key - and how to put a command exactly where you want it.

classic.text: **Double-click.** Select the line after which the command should come (1), then double-click the command in the **{{GroupEvents}}** list (2). The new line appears right below the selected one - here a `wait` after `camera ( MOVE )`. That is how the original BehavEd worked.
classic.unter: 1: the selected line. 2: the command in the list.

classic.text: **Insert key.** Click a command in the list once - it stays highlighted (1). Select a line in the tree (2) and press <kbd>Insert</kbd>. Handy when you add the same command several times: select, <kbd>Insert</kbd>, select, <kbd>Insert</kbd> ...
classic.unter: 1: the command stays selected in the list. 2: where it goes.

classic.text: **Drag.** Drag a command from the list (1) onto a line of the tree (2). While you drag, a line shows where it lands: above a line, below it, or - on the middle of an open block - inside the block.
classic.unter: Drag from the list (1) onto the tree (2).

classic.text: **Right-click.** Right-click a line in the tree: the submenus **{{GroupEvents}}** and **Macros** list every command; the one you click is inserted after that line - or into the block, if you right-clicked an open block.
classic.unter: The context menu of a line with its Events submenu.

touren.titel: Change the values of a command
touren.kurz: The event editor: lists, numbers, file fields, names from the map - and expressions such as get, tag and random.

classic.text: **Open the editor.** Double-click a line in the tree or select it and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>. The help text of the command stands on top; below it, every value has its own field.
classic.unter: The event editor for a camera command.

classic.text: **Fields for values.** Numbers, vectors and text are typed into their fields. A vector like a position has three numbers separated by spaces.
classic.unter: The value fields of camera ( MOVE ): a position and a time.

classic.text: **Fields with fixed choices.** Fields like `SET_TYPES` or `true` / `false` are lists you can also type into - start typing to filter the list. A value that is not in the list is allowed (mods bring their own), but it is marked **unknown**: check it for a typo.
classic.unter: The two list fields of set ( SET_WALKING, true ).

classic.text: **Files.** File fields have **{{EditorBrowse}}** to pick a file of the game and **{{EditorPlay}}** to play a sound or open a script. With a map loaded, an arrow next to name fields picks a name from the map.
classic.unter: A sound command: browse and play.

classic.text: **Expressions.** Some fields have **{{EditorHelper}}**: it builds an expression for you - **{{EditorGet}}** reads a variable (`get`), **{{EditorTag}}** the place or angles of a `ref_tag` (`tag`), **{{EditorRnd}}** a random number (`random`).
classic.unter: Helper next to a field of the camera command.

classic.text: **Free text.** Other fields have **{{EditorExpr}}**: it turns the field into free text, for anything the lists do not offer. **{{EditorRevert}}** goes back to a plain value.
classic.unter: Expr! next to the fields of affect.

classic.text: **Done.** **{{EditorOk}}** (<kbd>Enter</kbd>) writes the values into the script, **{{EditorCancel}}** (<kbd>Esc</kbd>) leaves everything as it was. Under each field you see the value it had before (**{{EditorWas}}**).
classic.unter: Ok and Cancel.

touren.titel: Move, copy and comment out lines
touren.kurz: Rearrange a script: select several lines, drag them, duplicate them, and switch lines off without deleting them.

classic.text: **Select.** Click a line in the tree. <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+click adds more lines, <kbd>Shift</kbd>+click selects everything between. Every button of the action column works on all selected lines at once.
classic.unter: Two selected lines.

classic.text: **Move.** Drag the selection to a new place - or press **{{ActMoveUp}}** / **{{ActMoveDown}}** in the action column (<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Up</kbd> / <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Down</kbd>) to move it one line. It stays inside its block. A block moves with everything inside it.
classic.unter: Move up and Move down.

classic.text: **Duplicate.** **{{ActClone}}** (<kbd>Space</kbd>) inserts a copy of the selection right below - the quickest way to a second camera shot or a second walk.
classic.unter: Duplicate.

classic.text: **Copy between scripts.** **{{ActCopy}}** (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd>) copies the selection. Switch to another tab, select a line and press **{{ActPaste}}** (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>V</kbd>): the commands are inserted below that line.
classic.unter: Copy and Paste.

classic.text: **Switch off without deleting.** **{{ActRem}}** (<kbd>Backspace</kbd>) turns the selected lines into comments: they stay in the script, but the game skips them. Press it again (or <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Backspace</kbd>) to switch them back on.
classic.unter: REM: the two lines are now comments.

touren.kurz: Turn the script into the .ibi the game runs, read the messages and jump to the line that is wrong.

classic.text: **Compile.** Press **{{Compile}}** at the bottom of the action column. It saves the `.txt` and writes the `.ibi` the game runs next to it. When it worked, the button flashes green.
classic.unter: The Compile button.

classic.text: **When it fails.** The button flashes red, and the first wrong line is selected in the tree - here an `if` with the comparison `~`, which ICARUS does not know.
classic.unter: Compile failed: the button and the selected wrong line.

classic.text: **Read the messages.** Click the counter in the status line at the bottom: the **{{MessagesTitle}}** window lists every message with its line and what is wrong.
classic.unter: The counters in the status line open the Messages window.

classic.text: **Fix and compile again.** Double-click the wrong line, correct the value - here the comparison: `=`, `<`, `>` or `!` - press **{{EditorOk}}** and **{{Compile}}** again.
classic.unter: The wrong value in the event editor.

touren.titel: Your first map: a room to walk in
touren.kurz: From an empty map to a room you can walk through in the game: brushes, textures, caulk, a light, the player start, the optimizer, building with the progress window, walking through it in the editor - and the .pk3 for the game.

classic.text: **Set up the game.** Switch the mode bar to **{{ViewMapEditor}}**. The editor uses the game the program is set up for; its folders come from the program settings. **{{KeLEdit}} > {{KeLPreferences}}**, page **{{KePgGame}}**, shows the game, page **{{KePgPaths}}** the engine path (empty: taken from the program's game folders).
classic.unter: {{KeLPreferences}}, page {{KePgPaths}}.

classic.text: **New map.** **{{KeLFile}} > {{KeLNewMap}}** starts an empty map - only the worldspawn. Zoom the 2D view out a little with the mouse wheel.
classic.unter: The {{KeLFile}} menu.

classic.text: **Draw a brush.** In the 2D top view, drag with the left mouse button from one corner to the other - here from -256 -256 to 256 256, a box 512 units wide. Its height comes from the work zone (at first -64 to 64).
classic.unter: The new brush, selected (red).

falsch.text: That made an entity. Press Ctrl+Z, then drag with the LEFT mouse button in the 2D view.

classic.text: **Make it taller.** <kbd>Num 1</kbd> switches the 2D view to the front view (XZ). Grab just above the top edge and drag up: the top face follows on the grid. Here to 192 - the room is now 256 high. <kbd>Num 7</kbd> goes back to the top view.
classic.unter: The front view: the brush is now 256 high.

falsch.text: That drew a second brush. Press Ctrl+Z and start the drag just above the top edge of the first one.

classic.text: **Texture.** Double-click a folder in the tree of the texture browser and click a texture with the left mouse button: every face of the selected brush gets it. Pick something without transparency for the walls.
classic.unter: The wall texture on all six faces.

falsch.text: Nothing is selected yet. Click the brush in a 2D view first, then the texture.

classic.text: **Hollow it out.** The toolbar button **{{KeCsgTitle}}** opens the CSG tool. Leave the thickness at 16 and switch the caulk button off for now (AutoCaulk does that later), then press **{{KeCsgTipPull}}**: six walls 16 thick grow outwards around the room, and the inside stays exactly the box you drew. The toolbar button **Room** (Make Room) does the same with the grid size as thickness.
classic.unter: {{KeCsgTitle}} with the caulk button off.

classic.text: **A floor texture.** In the front view, <kbd>Shift</kbd> + left click on the floor selects only the floor brush; click a floor texture in the browser. <kbd>Esc</kbd> clears the selection.
classic.unter: The hollow room: six wall brushes.

falsch.text: Nothing is selected yet. Click the brush in a 2D view first, then the texture.

classic.text: **A light.** Right-click inside the room in the 2D view: the entity menu opens. **light** asks for the intensity (300 is a good start) - **OK** places it where you clicked.
classic.unter: {{KeLiTitle}}.

falsch.text: That drew a brush. Press Ctrl+Z and click with the RIGHT mouse button.

classic.text: **Where the player starts.** Right-click near the floor: **info > info_player_start**. Without it the game does not know where to put the player. Its box stands on the floor.
classic.unter: The entity menu, submenu info.

falsch.text: That was another light. Right-click again and choose info > info_player_start.

classic.text: **Save.** **{{KeLFile}} > {{KeLSaveAs}}** - for example `meinekarte.map` in a folder `maps` of your own, outside the game folders. The name of the file becomes the name of the map in the game.
classic.unter: The saved room in the editor.

classic.text: **Caulk the outside.** Faces nobody can see still cost lightmap space and drawing time. Fly the camera into the room, drag a rectangle around the whole room with <kbd>Shift</kbd> + right mouse button in the top view and press <kbd>F4</kbd> (**{{KeLBrush}} > {{KeLAutoCaulkSelected}}**): every face that cannot be seen from inside becomes caulk. Building in caulk from the start works too: give new brushes the caulk texture and texture only the faces you see.
classic.unter: After AutoCaulk: the camera inside the room.

classic.text: **Check it.** **{{KeLBuild}} > {{KeOptMenue}}** counts the game's limits and looks for build problems before you compile. A green room has nothing to fix.
classic.unter: The optimizer for the tutorial room.

classic.text: **Build.** **{{KeLBuild}} > [Final] Fast** runs q3map2 three times - BSP, VIS and the light with bounce. The progress window shows the stage, the progress and the time left. If the map leaked, the console says so in red and a line in the 2D view shows the way out - see Map editor: compiling the map.
classic.unter: The progress window during the build.

classic.text: **Walk through it.** **{{KeLView}} > {{KeSpSpawn}}** and then **{{KeSpMenue}}** (<kbd>F6</kbd>): you stand at the info_player_start and walk with <kbd>W</kbd> <kbd>A</kbd> <kbd>S</kbd> <kbd>D</kbd>, jump with <kbd>Space</kbd>; <kbd>Esc</kbd> ends. This works even without compiling - the collision comes straight from the brushes (see Play in the editor).
classic.unter: Walking through the room in the editor.

classic.text: **Into the game.** **{{KeLBuild}} > {{KePkMenue}}** packs `maps/meinekarte.bsp` into `meinekarte.pk3` next to the .bsp. The program never writes into the game folders - copy the .pk3 yourself into `GameData/base` (Jedi Academy, Jedi Outcast) or into the folder of your mod (for example Movie Duels). Start the game, open the console with <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>~</kbd> and type `devmap meinekarte`.
classic.unter: {{KeLBuild}} with **{{KePkMenue}}** (not in NetRadiant-Custom).

touren.titel: Put a shot where you are looking
touren.kurz: Look around until the picture is right, then move a shot - or a new one - exactly there.

classic.text: **Fly to the view you want.** Hold the right mouse button in the map and fly with <kbd>W</kbd> <kbd>A</kbd> <kbd>S</kbd> <kbd>D</kbd> until the picture is right.
classic.unter: Your own view of the map.

falsch.text: No map is open yet. Load one first: {{MenuFile}} > {{MapLoad}} - or open a mission.

classic.text: **A new shot here.** Select the camera and press **{{CamNewShot}}**: a `camera ( MOVE )` and `camera ( PAN )` at your view are added after the selected shot.
classic.unter: New camera shot here in the camera panel.

falsch.text: No map is open yet. Load one first: {{MenuFile}} > {{MapLoad}} - or open a mission.
This script has no camera yet. Insert a camera command first ({{GroupEvents}} list: double-click camera) - or open a mission with a cutscene.
Select the camera first: click a camera shot on the map or the camera row in the timeline. Its buttons appear on the left.

classic.text: **Or move an existing one.** Select a shot in **{{CamShots}}** and press **{{CamSetToView}}**: its position and direction are replaced by your view - one undo step.
classic.unter: Set to view.

falsch.text: Select the camera first: click a camera shot on the map or the camera row in the timeline. Its buttons appear on the left.

classic.text: **Check.** **{{MapThroughCam}}** on the map toolbar shows what the selected shot sees, with its zoom and the black cinema bars.
classic.unter: Through camera on the toolbar.
